# KidsFirst: Calm Co-Parenting, Free

> The free co-parenting app with an AI Conflict Filter. Manage schedules, messages, expenses, and documents in one place. Started by a parent, built by a community, run for the mission – not for profit. Core co-parenting features are free, always. Available in Australia, New Zealand, and Singapore.

## About KidsFirst

KidsFirst is a free co-parenting app started by Vincent, a father who experienced
first-hand the damage that parental conflict causes children, and now built by a
community. It helps separated and divorced parents communicate calmly, share a
calendar, track expenses, and store documents in one place.

KidsFirst is founder-led and community-built, supported by AWS, and **not run to
make a profit** – any money it brings in goes back into keeping the core free and
helping more families. The core co-parenting features are free, always. Major
competitors (OurFamilyWizard, TalkingParents, 2houses) charge $100–300/year.

The core differentiator is the **AI Conflict Filter**: hostile messages are
reviewed by AI before sending and rewritten to remove aggressive language and
reduce escalation, so the receiving parent gets the logistics without the insult.
The Conflict Filter is the core of the product, not an add-on: it is always on
and cannot be switched off.

KidsFirst also rethinks how co-parents message. Most messaging apps put everything
into a single thread between two people, which works for casual chat but quickly
becomes a mess for co-parenting, where different topics – schooling, health,
handovers, expenses – need to be followed up separately. KidsFirst uses
**Topic-Based Threads**: each topic has its own thread, so co-parents can follow up
on each subject in its own place and conversations never get mixed up or buried.

Available on iOS and Android in Australia, New Zealand, and Singapore.

## Key features

- Shared messaging with the AI Conflict Filter
- Topic-Based Threads – a separate message thread per topic, so co-parents follow up on each subject without conversations getting mixed up
- Shared parenting calendar and scheduling
- Expense tracking and co-parenting records
- Shared document library
- Designed for separated or divorced parents, with the wellbeing of children as the north star

## How is it free?

KidsFirst is free because it's **not run to make a profit** – that's the
difference, not lower quality. Running costs are largely covered by AWS's startup
program, overheads are kept low, and the team is committed to keeping the core
free. The families who need calmer co-parenting most are often already paying for
lawyers, court, and a second home, so they shouldn't be priced out. Free is a
philosophy, not a discount. (Core co-parenting features are free, always; any
optional advanced features that cost real money to run may be offered on an
opt-in basis in future, never as profit and never for the essentials.)

## Who builds and funds it?

KidsFirst is founder-led and community-built, supported today by AWS (it
graduated the Sydney Founder Institute and runs on AWS credits), and is pursuing
grants and welcoming donations to grow. The team is working toward formal charity
registration. The service runs on durable AWS infrastructure in Australia, so it
doesn't depend on any one person.

## Is my data safe?

Yes – by design, not just by promise. KidsFirst does not sell or trade your data,
does not run ads, and never uses your messages to train AI. Personal details (such
as names and contact information) are automatically removed from a message before
it reaches the AI model – best-effort and always improving – so the filter works on
the tone of a message, not on who your family is. Your messages are processed only
to run the Conflict Filter, within AWS. **No one on the team can access your private
records: it's enforced by how the app is built.**
